what: Loading a proc macro's compiled module is a write into the front end's database, so it waits for and cancels every reader in flight, whether or not it uses that macro; the outside audit of 2026-11-13 ties the `blaze check --workspace` stall at 920 of 3,406 units to it. Separately, a call's kept result is trusted by a per-module Verdict (Unseen/Stateless/Settles/Stateful) guessed from behaviour, not by a key that names the state the call starts from.
cost: every macro crate that finishes compiling stops the whole front end once; a stateful macro's kept output is right only while the verdict's guess holds
cause: the expander table is an input of the database, set when a module appears, instead of a record the call reads by a key known before the module exists; and a call's key leaves out the expander's starting state
class: late-arriving work products installed by mutating shared state that unrelated readers depend on, and cache keys that leave out an input the value depends on (state carried between calls)
prevention: the module is a record keyed by its crate's unit key and reached through one seam (blaze_expansion::modules::Modules) that parks only its users; the call's key holds StateIn, and a stateful module's calls are chained in source order (blaze_expansion::chain)
workaround: none in this lane: the crate is written, the wiring is another lane's
fix: crates/blaze-expansion (records, machine, seam, chain, with simulations whose plants include the global write and state carried across calls); wiring not yet
